documents.title: Academic Honesty Policy
documents.summary: Pomona's Student Handbook academic honesty policy names 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' among the ways students misrepresent others' ideas or language as their own, leaving approval of AI use to courses. The rest is a general misconduct procedure that would govern AI cases: faculty report to the Vice President of Student Affairs, a preliminary meeting with the student, a clear-and-convincing standard at hearings, and sanctions from assignment penalties to expulsion.

units.anchor: failing to use citations, unapproved use of artificial intelligence
units.policy: In independently prepared projects and assignments, unapproved use of artificial intelligence is an example of intentionally representing the ideas or language of others as one's own.

units.anchor: they must submit a complaint directly to the Vice-President of Student Affairs/Dean of Students

units.policy: Faculty who believe a student violated academic standards must submit a complaint directly to the Vice President of Student Affairs/Dean of Students.

units.anchor: All charges must be brought within ten (10) academic days of the discovery
units.policy: All academic dishonesty charges must be brought within ten academic days of the faculty member's discovery of the alleged violation.

units.policy: For an alleged violation, the Vice President informs the student of the charges and their rights and schedules a preliminary meeting with the student and faculty member.

units.anchor: Any sanctions must be course-specific—such as a failing grade on an assignment.
units.policy: Sanctions in the first-violation process must be course-specific, such as a failing grade on an assignment.

units.anchor: If the violation and resulting penalty could lead to failing the course
units.policy: If the violation and resulting penalty could lead to failing the course, the incident should be referred to a hearing panel.

units.policy: The Academic Discipline Board uses a clear-and-convincing evidence standard to determine responsibility.

units.policy: Possible sanctions include a lower grade, loss of credit, or F on an assignment, an F in the course, make-up work, suspension, loss of honors, or expulsion.

units.policy: For students enrolling from Fall 2026, non-suspension/expulsion violations and sanctions are reportable to employers and graduate schools for 3 years after graduation.

documents.title: Computer Science AI Policy Tier System
tiers: Tier 1: See syllabus for allowed usage
Tier 2: Use in any way with required attribution
documents.summary: Pomona CS's pilot (Fall 2026) department-wide AI tier system assigns every CS course to one of four tiers, from Tier 0 (no AI at all, including brainstorming, study guides, code snippets, or revision; only passive spell/grammar checkers) to Tier 3 (open use without credit, AI output counted as the student's own work). Tier 1 lets instructors curb AI with syllabus-defined exceptions, Tier 2 allows any use with attribution like a co-author, and using AI out of line with a course's tier violates the departmental honor policy; the system will be revisited regularly.

units.anchor: provide a unified system and increase clarity about what AI usages are allowed or disallowed
units.policy: The document provides a unified system to increase clarity about which AI uses are allowed or disallowed across all Pomona Computer Science classes.

units.anchor: a program we are piloting in Fall 2026; we plan to revisit it regularly
units.frag_start: This is a program we are piloting

units.policy: Because AI technologies advance rapidly, the document focuses on general usage rather than specific tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grammarly, etc.).

units.anchor: outlines the four tiers of allowed use that a course can fall under
units.policy: Each course falls under one of four tiers of allowed use, from least to most permissive: no usage, see syllabus, any use with attribution, completely open use.

units.policy: Using AI in a way that does not align with a course's tier is a violation of the Departmental Academic Honor Policy.

units.policy: (Tier 1) The tier gives flexibility to instructors who primarily want to curb AI use but may make exceptions tailored to their course's learning objectives.

units.policy: (Tier 1 example) A course might allow AI for study purposes (clarifying questions, additional examples, study guides) but prohibit it while completing assignments and exams.

documents.title: Academic Honesty Policy (Computer Science Department)
documents.summary: The CS department's academic honesty policy (revised August 2026) requires independent work not based on sources unapproved by instructors, explicitly including AI tools, and makes all CS courses follow the pilot AI tier system. It bans copying solutions from AI tools, requires citing permitted AI in papers, forbids using course materials as AI prompts unless allowed, uses software to detect similarity and AI-generated content, and sets penalties (zero plus at least a half-letter reduction, then referral to the Academic Discipline Board).

notes: Reconciled consensus of two independent coders (v2 dry run). Collection notes: University layer: no Pomona-wide AI guidance page found; the Student Handbook Academic Honesty Policy contains one AI clause ('unapproved use of artificial intelligence') and is included on that basis. CSWIM 'about' page (cited by a third-party aggregator as Pomona's AI statement) contains no AI policy text (excluded). Pomona has no school/college layer and no other computing unit besides the CS department. Course layer: CS 54 and CS 140 have a one-line AI rule; CS 101's linked 'MZ-AI-policy.pdf' returns 404 (inaccessible). Reconciliation details and the reason for each resolved disagreement are in v2/dryrun/agreement_pomona.json.
